meta.source: AMTROL, Sizing the Therm-X-Trol (form MC10007, 03/19): expansion factor table and design pressure factor equation; AMTROL Therm-X-Trol specifications and Quick Sizing Charts (form MC8520, 04/22); Washington State Department of Health, Protect Your Water Heater from Thermal Expansion (2025)
meta.notes: Sizing method: expanded water = water heater gallons x expansion factor (from 40 °F to the tank setting); required tank volume = expanded water x design pressure factor, where DPF = (maximum allowed pressure + 14.7) / (maximum allowed pressure - static supply pressure), pressures in psig. A tank fits when its total volume is at least the required volume and its maximum acceptance volume is at least the expanded water. Tank classes are one manufacturer's residential models; other brands publish their own acceptance volumes, so check the spec sheet of the tank you buy. Expansion factors between table temperatures are interpolated linearly (our choice).

amtrol-sizing.title: Sizing the Therm-X-Trol: for pressurization and expansion control of hot water systems (MC10007, 03/19)
quotes: Tv = Design Pressure Factor x expanded water
DPF = (Max. Allow. Pressure + 14.7) / (Max. Allow. Pressure - Line Pressure)
Table 1 Expansion Factor ... *Based on initial temperature of 40˚F.
When sizing a Therm-X-Trol, the unit must meet the calculated expanded water and total tank volume.
The Therm-X-Trol air pressure should be equal to static line pressure.
Standard Therm-X-Trol tanks are shipped at 40 psi ... it is necessary to match the precharge to the incoming supply pressure before installation.
It is necessary to install the Therm-X-Trol on the cold water supply after the backflow preventer.
Examples of one-way devices include: Backflow Preventers (BFP's), Check Valves, Pressure Reducing Valves (PRV's)

amtrol-chart.title: Therm-X-Trol water heater expansion tanks: specifications and Quick Sizing Charts (MC8520, 04/22)
quotes: ST-5: tank volume 2.0 gal, max. acceptance volume 0.9 gal; ST-12: 4.4 gal, 3.2 gal; ST-25V: 10.3 gal, 10.3 gal; ST-30V: 14.0 gal, 11.3 gal
Maximum Working Pressure: 150 psig. Factory Pre-charge: ST-5 and ST-12: 50 PSIG
Sizing based on: 40°F incoming water temperature; 150 psi T&P safety relief valve; Precharge equal to static supply pressure

wa-doh.title: Protect Your Water Heater from Thermal Expansion (2025)
quotes: The thermal expansion tank controls the increased pressure generated within the normal operating temperature range of the water heater. The small tank with a sealed compressible air cushion provides a space to store and hold the additional expanded water volume.
The T & P Valve is normally pre-set at 125 psi or 150 psi.

For public health protection, the water purveyor may require the installation of a check valve or backflow preventer downstream of the water meter. In these situations, it is essential that a T & P Valve and thermal expansion tank be properly installed

watts-etp.title: Expansion Tank Sizing Calculator (Potable)
quotes: Initial Pressure: typically does not exceed 80 PSI as per UPC plumbing code.
Air pre-charge should match Initial Pressure. Never exceed 80 PSI pre-charge!
Final Pressure: Initial Pressure plus 50%; should not exceed 85% of the T&P relief valve rating.
Initial Temperature: set to 90°F; use lower values only if the entire contents of the water heater are drained on each use.

defaults.maxPsiNote: The relief valve setting; AMTROL's quick charts assume a 150 psi relief valve. Many installers design to a lower maximum for margin, which gives a larger tank.
defaults.headroomNote: Our rule: when the required volume or the expanded water is within 15% of the chosen tank's limit, we also name the next size as a safer pick. AMTROL's own chart picks the larger size in most such borderline cases.
